title: The Wounded Angel
source: Ateneum Art Museum, Finnish National Gallery, Helsinki (public domain). Full resolution from Wikimedia Commons: File:The Wounded Angel - Hugo Simberg.jpg (8537 x 6870 px as given in the brief; Wikimedia unreachable from the cloud, size not re-checked 2026-10-24)
caption: Two boys, one blindfolded angel, and a painter who refused to explain. Look closer at the boy on the right. #angel #mystery #symbolism #painting #hiddendetails
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-24, Wikipedia EN (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wounded_Angel): Hugo Simberg, Finnish symbolist, 1903, oil, 127 x 154 cm, Ateneum Helsinki; boys carry an injured angel with a bandaged forehead/eyes and a bloodied wing, bearers in sombre clothing; setting Eläintarha park, Helsinki, Töölönlahti Bay in the background; angel clutches snowdrops, 'symbolic of healing and rebirth'; several charity institutions were in Eläintarha, the boys carry her toward the Blind Girls' School and the Home for Cripples; Simberg had suffered from meningitis, the painting a source of strength during his recovery; he declined to explain it, viewers should draw their own conclusions; 2006 Ateneum vote named it Finland's 'national painting'.

VERIFIED, DailyArt Magazine (dailyartmagazine.com/wounded-angel-by-hugo-simberg): eyes bandaged, wing bloodied, snowdrops; Eläintarha with Töölönlahti Bay, 'The pathway along Töölönlahti Bay remains there to this day'; Blind Girls' School and Home for Cripples; meningitis; 'Simberg himself hated to explain his works and he always refused to do so'. Yle (yle.fi/a/3-10247437): voted national painting in 2006.

CORRECTED, not as in the brief: 'one boy looks straight at you' is contradicted by Wikipedia EN ('gaze fixated beyond and to the right of the viewer'). Slide 6 says only that he turns his head out of the painting, 'almost at us'.

CAUTIOUS: 'while recovering from meningitis' follows Wikipedia ('source of strength during his recovery') and DailyArt ('helped him recover'); the exact timing of the illness vs the painting is not stated in the sources read. Slide 8 'The boys seem to be heading there' is phrased softer than Wikipedia, which states it as fact; it is an interpretation of the route.

THEORY / rhetorical, flagged: slide 6 'Asking for help, or accusing?' is a question to the viewer, not a claim about Simberg's intent. Snowdrops as 'spring's first flowers' is general botany, not from an art source.
VERIFIED, not used (word budget): a larger version was painted for the Tampere Cathedral frescoes (1905-06); praised at the 1903 Ateneum autumn exhibition.

slides.headline: Two boys. One fallen angel. Zero answers.
Helsinki, 1903
slides.text: Helsinki, 1903. Two boys carry a wounded angel on a stretcher. Hugo Simberg never explained it. So let's follow the clues.

slides.headline: Blindfolded, head bowed
slides.text: First, the angel. A bandage covers her eyes, one wing hangs damaged, her head is bowed. She barely holds on to the stretcher.

slides.headline: Look at her hand
slides.text: But look at her hand. She clutches a few snowdrops, spring's first flowers, often read as a sign of healing and rebirth.

slides.headline: The boy in black
slides.text: Meanwhile, the boy in front, dressed in sombre black, stares at the ground and keeps walking. He never looks back.

slides.headline: The boy who turns
slides.text: But the second boy turns his head out of the painting, almost at us. A hard stare. Asking for help, or accusing?

slides.headline: A real Helsinki park
slides.text: And the place is real: Eläintarha park in Helsinki, beside Töölönlahti Bay. That waterside path is still there today. But where are they going?

slides.headline: Toward the blind school
slides.text: Back then, charities stood in this park, including a school for blind girls and a home for disabled people. The boys seem headed there.

slides.headline: Finland's national painting
slides.text: Simberg painted it while recovering from meningitis. In a 2006 Ateneum vote, it became Finland's national painting. What do you think happened to her?
